subject: English
description: Sentence-ordering puzzles; identify the topic sentence, opener, link, conclusion

questions.stem:
Arrange in the most logical order:
P. The result was a steady decline in pollinator populations.
Q. Bees and butterflies depend on diverse flowering plants for food.
R. Industrial agriculture has replaced these plants with single-crop monocultures.
S. Pollinator decline now threatens the very crops monoculture was supposed to expand.

options.option_text: Q, R, P, S
R, Q, P, S
Q, P, R, S
P, Q, R, S

questions.explanation: Q opens with the general fact (bees + diverse plants). R introduces the change (monocultures replaced diversity). P is the consequence (decline). S is the irony / resolution (decline threatens the very crops). The chain is fact → change → consequence → larger irony. Q-R-P-S. Distractor 2 starts with R but R requires the prior context Q first.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Arrange in the most logical order:
P. Yet the deeper question — why we forget — remained.
Q. For decades, neuroscientists assumed memory worked like a hard drive.
R. The brain, they realised, did not store memory — it reconstructed it.
S. Recent imaging studies overturned that assumption entirely.

options.option_text: Q, S, R, P
Q, R, S, P
P, Q, R, S
S, Q, R, P

questions.explanation: Q sets up the old assumption. S says recent studies overturned it. R explains what those studies showed. P closes with the unresolved deeper question. Q-S-R-P. Distractor 2 puts R before S — but R is the conclusion of S's studies. Distractor 3 starts with P, which makes no sense without prior setup.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Arrange in the most logical order:
P. The smell of monsoon rain on dry earth has a name — petrichor.
Q. The compound responsible is geosmin, produced by soil microbes.
R. Once airborne, geosmin reaches the human nose in startlingly small concentrations.
S. We can detect just five parts per trillion — sharper than a shark's sense of blood in water.

options.option_text: P, Q, R, S
Q, P, R, S
P, R, Q, S
S, R, Q, P

questions.explanation: P introduces the phenomenon (petrichor). Q identifies the compound. R describes how it travels. S quantifies our sensitivity, with a vivid comparison. Topic → mechanism → behaviour → striking detail. P-Q-R-S. Distractor 2 starts with Q (the compound) before introducing the phenomenon, which is unnatural.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Arrange in the most logical order:
P. By the time the contract was signed, both sides had stopped trusting each other.
Q. The negotiations began with cautious goodwill.
R. Each new clause introduced fresh suspicion.
S. Lawyers spent more time drafting protections than drafting the deal.

options.option_text: Q, R, S, P
P, Q, R, S
Q, S, R, P
R, S, Q, P

questions.explanation: Q starts with goodwill (the beginning). R describes the gradual deterioration (each clause adds suspicion). S is the consequence (lawyers focus on protection). P is the end-state (no trust). Beginning → deterioration → consequence → end. Q-R-S-P. Distractor 2 puts P (the end) first — illogical. Distractor 3 reverses R and S.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Arrange in the most logical order:
P. They turned out to be three orders of magnitude older than any human migration trail.
Q. Researchers used radiocarbon to date the charcoal remains in the cave.
R. A team of cavers exploring a remote Indonesian cave found ancient hand stencils on a wall.
S. The discovery rewrote textbook chronology of the earliest known figurative art.

options.option_text: R, Q, P, S
R, P, Q, S
Q, R, P, S
S, R, Q, P

questions.explanation: R is the discovery event (first sentence). Q describes the analysis. P reports the surprising result. S states the larger implication. Discovery → analysis → result → implication. R-Q-P-S. Distractor 2 puts P (result) before Q (analysis) — backwards. Distractor 3 starts with the analysis without first introducing what was found.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Arrange in the most logical order:
P. Solar panels on the roof now power the whole farmhouse.
Q. The Patil family had grown tired of erratic grid electricity in their village.
R. Within six months, their monthly power bill had dropped to zero.
S. They decided to invest in a small rooftop solar system.

options.option_text: Q, S, P, R
P, Q, S, R
Q, P, R, S
S, Q, P, R

questions.explanation: Q is the problem (erratic grid). S is the decision. P is the implementation. R is the outcome. Problem → decision → implementation → outcome. Q-S-P-R. Distractor 2 leads with P (the result) before introducing the problem. Distractor 3 places P before S — installation before deciding to install. Distractor 4 puts the decision before the problem that motivated it.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Arrange in the most logical order:
P. But the engine of self-doubt rarely runs out of fuel.
Q. Imposter syndrome makes accomplished people feel like frauds.
R. Even after objective achievements, the feeling persists.
S. Therapy can help break the loop, but the doubt itself is part of being human.

options.option_text: Q, R, P, S
Q, P, R, S
P, Q, R, S
Q, R, S, P

questions.explanation: Q defines the phenomenon. R says it persists despite achievement. P emphasises that the doubt rarely stops. S offers an outlook (therapy helps but it's part of being human). Definition → persistence → emphasis → outlook. Q-R-P-S. Distractor 2 swaps R and P. Distractor 4 ends on P, which leaves the reader on a negative note rather than the more measured S.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The sentences P, Q, R, and S, when arranged properly, form a coherent paragraph. P. The dew on the grass sparkled in the early morning light. Q. She decided to take a walk before the rest of the city awoke. R. By the time she returned home, she felt calm and refreshed. S. Birds began to chirp softly as she stepped into the street. Which sequence is correct?

options.option_text: The order Q – P – S – R is most logical
The order Q – S – P – R is most logical
The order S – Q – P – R is most logical
The order P – Q – S – R is most logical

questions.explanation: Q → S → P → R is correct: Q establishes the motivation (she decides to walk); S captures the act of stepping out while birds chirp; P describes a mid-walk sensory observation (dew); R is the concluding return. Option A (QPSR) is wrong because P is a static observation that occurs during the walk, whereas S (stepping into the street) must precede any walk-time detail.

questions.stem: Arrange sentences P, Q, R, S to form a coherent paragraph. P. After several failed attempts, the clay finally took shape between the apprentice's palms. Q. The wheel spun steadily as the master centred a fresh lump of clay. R. The apprentice smoothed the rim with a wet cloth and set the piece aside to dry. S. A young man sat at the wheel's edge, watching his master's every movement. Which sequence is correct?

options.option_text: The order Q – S – P – R is most logical
The order P – Q – S – R is most logical
The order S – Q – P – R is most logical
The order Q – P – S – R is most logical

questions.explanation: S → Q → P → R is correct: S introduces the apprentice observing the master; Q shows what the apprentice is watching (master spinning clay on the wheel); P records the apprentice's own attempt succeeding after failures; R is the finishing step. Option A (QSPR) is tempting but places the wheel in motion before the apprentice has even been introduced as an observer, breaking narrative causality.

questions.stem: Arrange sentences P, Q, R, S into a coherent paragraph. P. Once a product receives a GI tag, only authorised producers from that region may use the name commercially. Q. India has over 400 registered Geographical Indications spanning textiles, food products, and handicrafts. R. A Geographical Indication is a sign that identifies a product as originating from a specific geographic region. S. This legal protection helps artisans command better prices and prevents rampant counterfeiting. Which sequence is correct?

options.option_text: The order Q – R – P – S is most logical
The order R – Q – P – S is most logical
The order R – P – Q – S is most logical
The order P – R – Q – S is most logical

questions.explanation: R → Q → P → S is correct: R defines the concept (GI tag); Q establishes India's scale of registrations; P details the legal exclusivity mechanism that makes the tag valuable; S concludes with economic benefits. Option A (QRPS) opens with a statistic before the concept has been defined, violating the define-then-exemplify logic standard in formal expository paragraphs.

questions.stem: Arrange sentences P, Q, R, S to form a well-structured paragraph. P. These ecosystems act as natural filters, removing toxins before they reach open water bodies. Q. Wetlands are among the most biologically productive environments on Earth. R. Rapid urban expansion and agricultural encroachment have drastically reduced their area worldwide. S. Conservation programmes now work to restore drained wetlands and revive lost habitats. Which is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The order P – Q – R – S is most logical
The order Q – R – P – S is most logical
The order Q – P – R – S is most logical
The order R – Q – P – S is most logical

questions.explanation: Q → P → R → S is correct: Q introduces the subject; P explains one key ecological function (filtration), elaborating on Q's claim; R presents the threat (habitat loss); S offers the resolution (conservation). Option B (QRPS) is wrong because R describes the threat before P has established the ecological value being threatened, making the loss feel unmotivated.

questions.stem: Arrange sentences P, Q, R, S into a coherent paragraph. P. Sanskrit is regarded as the progenitor of many modern Indian languages, including Hindi and Bengali. Q. The Devanagari script, used for both Sanskrit and Hindi, was standardised roughly around the 11th century CE. R. Despite having fewer than 25,000 fluent speakers today, Sanskrit remains active in religious rituals and certain legal texts. S. Scholars argue that reintroducing Sanskrit in schools could strengthen students' grasp of regional languages. Which is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The order Q – P – R – S is most logical
The order P – Q – R – S is most logical
The order P – R – Q – S is most logical
The order Q – R – P – S is most logical

questions.explanation: P → Q → R → S is correct: P establishes Sanskrit's linguistic significance; Q adds the historical dimension of its script; R pivots to the present-day status using a concessive 'Despite'; S presents the policy argument that naturally follows from R's observation. Option C (PRQS) is wrong because it jumps to present-day decline before providing the historical script context in Q, disrupting chronological flow.

questions.stem: Arrange sentences P, Q, R, S into the most logically coherent paragraph. P. H.L.A. Hart argued that law is fundamentally a system of rules, not necessarily connected to moral principles. Q. This long-running debate between legal positivism and natural law theory continues to shape modern jurisprudence. R. Lon Fuller countered that law must embody an inner morality — consisting of clarity, consistency, and prospectivity. S. Ronald Dworkin later pressed further, claiming that principles and rights, not just rules, determine legal outcomes. Which sequence is correct?

options.option_text: The order Q – P – R – S is most logical
The order P – S – R – Q is most logical
The order R – P – S – Q is most logical
The order P – R – S – Q is most logical

questions.explanation: P → R → S → Q is correct: P states Hart's positivism (the thesis); R presents Fuller's counter-argument (antithesis); S adds Dworkin's further challenge chronologically ('later'); Q is the concluding meta-sentence — 'this long-running debate' can only refer back to positions already stated. Option A (QPRS) is a classic trap: Q's phrase 'this long-running debate' presupposes the reader knows what is being debated, making Q logically impossible as an opener.

questions.stem: Arrange sentences P, Q, R, S into the most logically coherent paragraph. P. Working memory, typically limited to about four discrete items, serves as a bottleneck for all conscious reasoning. Q. Long-term memory, unlike working memory, has no known upper capacity limit, though retrieval failures are common. R. Memory researchers distinguish between declarative memory, which encodes facts and events, and procedural memory, which encodes skills. S. This distinction has direct clinical relevance: Alzheimer's disease erodes declarative memory far earlier and more severely than procedural memory. Which sequence is correct?

options.option_text: The order P – Q – R – S is most logical
The order R – Q – P – S is most logical
The order R – P – Q – S is most logical
The order Q – R – P – S is most logical

questions.explanation: R → P → Q → S is correct: R introduces the declarative/procedural distinction (the paragraph's organising concept); P introduces working memory and its capacity constraint; Q then explicitly contrasts long-term memory 'unlike working memory', requiring P to have appeared first; S applies the full taxonomy clinically. Option B (RQPS) is the most tempting wrong answer because Q follows R naturally, but Q's opening phrase 'unlike working memory' makes no sense before P has introduced working memory as a defined term.
